title: Darius begins Persepolis
summary: Darius I began the great terrace at Persepolis around 518 BCE. Later Achaemenid rulers added palaces, reception halls and carved reliefs to this royal complex in present-day Iran.

A monumental centre represents political power selectively. The architecture and tribute imagery illuminate royal display, while the site’s foundation must remain distinct from the beginning of the Achaemenid Empire.
